extracted.intended_audience: Indian agents preparing annual reports for the Department of Indian Affairs
extracted.subtask_description: Annual operational report by a U.S. Indian agency agent describing population rolls, agriculture, supplies, buildings, education, sanitation, police, improvements, and recommendations to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population rolls and census breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the number of Indians on the roll, broken down by band/group and by sex and age categories (men, women, boys, girls), with aggregate totals and comparison to last annual report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include transfers in/out, absentees, 'absent without leave and unaccounted for', and note approximate accuracy if exact census not possible. Example wording: 'The number of Indians now on the roll is 1,292 : Arickarees, 636 ; Gros Ventres, 364 ; Mandans, 252.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Births and deaths statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report births and deaths during the year (raw counts) and any relevant causes or reporting issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State totals, note late reporting (e.g., deaths reported after medicine men failed), and compute death rate change where possible. Example: 'There have been 62 births and 49 deaths during the past twelve months.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural acreage and yields (agency and Indians)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail acres cultivated by the agency and by Indians, broken down by crop (wheat, oats, corn, potatoes, beans, squashes, etc.) and provide estimated or actual yields per crop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide totals, increases over last year, reasons for shortfalls (drought, late equipment), and list per-family or per-person production when relevant. Example table-style listings of names/locations and acres cultivated are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency farm operations and production
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe agency farm acreage, crops planted, quantities produced for feed/seed, hay tonnage, and whether purchases of wood or forage were necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include acres newly added and output used for agency stock and seed. Example: 'During the year 13 acres of new land was added to agency farm... Eighty-five tons of hay were put up for agency use.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation and hauling metrics with economic valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Record amounts of freight hauled by Indians (pounds/tons), distances hauled, rates paid or saved, and money received or saved by government and Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give specific quantities and unit rates, and compute totals/savings. Example: 'they have hauled ... 352,270 pounds ... reckoning ... 65 cents per 100 pounds ... saved to the department and themselves $2,289.75.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Lumber, timber, and wood production and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Report quantities of logs cut, feet of lumber produced, cords of wood cut/hailed, rails produced, and wood supplied for contractors or agency needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include average distances hauled, payments per cord (cutting vs cutting+hauling), and use of lumber in buildings/fences. Example: 'They also cut and hauled to mill 742 oak logs, aggregating 37,500 feet of lumber, cut 665 cords of wood ... received $1 per cord for cutting and $3 per cord for cutting and hauling.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock and livestock inventory and suitability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Give counts of bulls, cows, yearlings, calves, yoke of work oxen, and total cattle owned; assess whether the reservation is adapted to stock-raising and recommend appropriate herd sizes per family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include historical issuance of stock, increases, and a reasoned recommendation (e.g., 'Each family should have from one to four milk cows'). Note climatic/forage constraints and whether stock-raising is profitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship and trades training status
rubrics_metrics.description: List apprentices (number), trades being learned (blacksmith, carpenter, etc.), tenure at trade, continuity of training, and assessment of progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note interruptions (if any) and provide qualitative assessment: 'have progressed satisfactorily', 'about three years ... now quite handy at their work.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Police force composition and performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report organization of Indian police (numbers, ranks), frequency/quality of execution of orders, public attitude toward service, and operational reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State dates of organization, reorganizations, problems (intimidation, unreliability), and whether orders are 'promptly executed'. Example: 'The police force ... consists of 20 Indians ... All orders issued to the police are promptly executed by them.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious and missionary activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe missionary supervision, clergy and lay workers present, mission chapel services (frequency and attendance), and sacramental statistics (e.g., baptisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report clergy names/denominations, attendance trends, adult vs child participation, and whether traditional practices (medicine dance) are declining. Example: 'Religious services are held ... the reverend pastor reports 60 baptisms during the year.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Education: schools, attendance, and language instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide data on schools (day and boarding), enrollment, largest and average monthly attendance, language(s) taught, discipline measures, boarding arrangements, and recommendations about school types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give attendance statistics (enrolled, largest average, average during year), comment on parental interest and irregular attendance, and state preferences (e.g., 'The English language is taught exclusively in the school' and preference for boarding schools over day/camp schools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary and public health reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report sanitary condition (presence/absence of epidemics), number treated by physician, deaths under treatment, causes of disease (e.g., improper food preparation), and trends in reliance on 'medicine men' vs physicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include counts treated and mortality figures, note improvements (e.g., death rate diminished), and behavioral changes in health-seeking ('steadily gaining confidence in the white medicine man').

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey status and land-allotment recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on the need for completion of reservation survey, call for prompt completion as required by treaty, and recommend land subdivision (e.g., division of timbered townships into forty-acre tracts) to resolve disputed timber claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain administrative harms caused by lack of survey (disputed timber claims) and expected benefits (security of ownership, encouragement of cultivation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rations policy and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the system of issuing rations (criticize gratuitous issues), and recommend a policy: gradual diminution, restrict issues to busy working months, or cease gratuitous issues after harvest until spring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale linking rations to improvidence and hindered labor; suggest transitional allowances to encourage cultivation and boarding school attendance. Example: 'The system of issuing rations to Indians is a wrong one ... gradually diminish ... issue during busy working months.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory and condition of agency buildings and improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: List agency buildings with dimensions and current condition (issue-house, meat-house, school-house, blacksmith shop, carpenter shop, offices, warehouses, mills, dwellings, barns), and report new construction or repairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include whether buildings are frame or log, usage (issue-house used for storing commissary supplies), and ongoing projects (e.g., grist-mill in course of erection). Give specifics of size/condition as evidence of agency capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplies, issues, and subsistence quality/delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe subsistence supplies furnished (quality, abundance), delivery timeliness, method of issuance (weekly, per capita), and storage/weighting practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on particular items (e.g., 'The beef was particularly good'), frequency of issues ('Issues are made weekly on Saturday forenoon'), and equitable distribution practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employes: staffing and labor organization
rubrics_metrics.description: List agency employes (white and Indian) by role and number (physician, clerk, farmer, carpenter, blacksmith, laborers, interpreters, herders, apprentices), including irregular/seasonal labor usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain workload (repairs to houses, wagons, implements), note reliance on Indian labor for harvesting/cutting timber, and the need for certain roles to maintain agency operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime, grievances, and dispute reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report known crimes committed within the tribe, notable offenses by outsiders, existing grievances (e.g., trader vs railroad company), and disputes over use of shared implements or property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note frequency/absence of crime, give concrete examples, and flag causes of grievance and their political implications. Example: 'during the year no known crime has been committed within the tribe ... the only offense recorded is one committed by an Indian from another agency.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation boundaries and enlargement requests
rubrics_metrics.description: State treaty-defined reservation boundaries, record Indian claims/disputes about boundaries, and recommend enlargement to include specific geographic resources (rivers, bends) for wood, water, and arable land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide geographic detail and justification (e.g., need for wood and arable land) and discuss likely settlement moves by parts of the tribe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of 'civilization' and social change
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe observable indicators: housing improvements (floors, shingles), construction of stables, adoption of white farming/market practices, decline of traditional ceremonies (Sun Dance, medicine dance), and changing attitudes toward labor and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualitative narrative linking material improvements and behavioral changes to policy/contacts (railroad, settlers) and note positive/negative effects (chiefship obstructions, influence of separation from villages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of shared implements and machinery
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventory agricultural implements (wagons, plows, grain-seeders, harrows, mowing-machines, reapers, threshing-machine) and report issues in equitable distribution, disputes over loans, and effects on productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give counts, note problems (loaned mower retained by borrower), and recommend management practices to reduce disputes that burden the agent's time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of agency projects as incentives to labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe building projects (houses, granary, grist-mill, stable) structured to encourage labor by requiring recipients to furnish materials (e.g., oak logs) and rewarding the most industrious with best housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain policy intent: civilize and incentivize labor by tying improvements to contribution of materials and work; report outcomes (industrious provided with best houses first).
